caption:
A report out today surveying 100 India GCC leaders found AI deployed nearly everywhere — and productivity gains still under 15%.

The tooling isn't the bottleneck. The transmission is.

You can run the model, read the output, and form a sound judgement by 9am IST. Then at 7pm you join a call where leadership sits three timezones away, and you have four minutes to make them believe you. That is where the gain is lost — not in the stack.

Being believed is a learnable discipline. Bearing: how you hold yourself before you speak. Tone: steady, low, unhurried, no upward lilt at the end of a statement of fact. Silence: the two seconds after your recommendation that you do not fill with qualifiers.

Thirty-five years of military command taught me that an order delivered without conviction is not an order. It's a suggestion. Most mid-career managers are delivering suggestions and wondering why nothing moves.

Fix the delivery.

topic.title: GCCs have AI everywhere, under 15% productivity gain
topic.angle: For mid-career managers inside India's GCCs, technical capability is no longer the differentiator — being believed when you narrate judgment to a leadership team in another timezone is, and that's bearing and tone, not tooling.
topic.why_now: The Embark report surveying 100 India GCC leaders published today (23 Oct 2026) and will be covered across Indian business media for several days.

rationale: A stark, text-only slate matches the no-nonsense command tone and lets the report's contrast — ubiquitous AI, flat productivity — land without decoration.
